title: Israel Kills Hamas Deputy Education Minister in Third Night of Gaza Strikes
excerpt: At least nine Palestinians were killed overnight, medics said, as Israel pressed a campaign of targeted killings and Hamas weighed its response under a ceasefire that has not stopped the violence.
body:
• Israeli airstrikes and gunfire killed at least nine Palestinians in Gaza overnight, medics said, in a third consecutive night of attacks despite the year-old ceasefire.
  • Among the dead was Khaled Abu Nada, Hamas's deputy minister of education, killed with his wife in a strike on their apartment in Deir al-Balah; he was the third senior Hamas official killed since Tuesday.
  • Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel has killed about 80 Hamas militants in the past month and pledged the targeted killings will continue.
  • Hamas called the killings a breach of the ceasefire and blamed the US-backed Board of Peace for failing to stop them, while Washington urges Netanyahu to proceed with the ceasefire plan.

Israeli airstrikes and gunfire killed at least nine Palestinians in Gaza overnight, medics said, including the Hamas-appointed deputy minister of education, in a third consecutive night of air attacks despite a one-year-old ceasefire, Reuters reported.

Medics said an Israeli airstrike hit an apartment in Deir al-Balah in central Gaza on Thursday, killing Khaled Abu Nada, the deputy Gaza education minister, and his wife. Two other airstrikes killed six people in the Tuffah neighbourhood and the Beach refugee camp in Gaza City, medics added, and Israeli gunfire later killed a 62-year-old man in the eastern Bureij refugee camp. The Israeli military did not immediately comment on those seven reported deaths.

A campaign of targeted killings

Abu Nada was the third senior Hamas official Israel has killed since Tuesday, after two senior security officials. On Wednesday, Israel struck and killed Muhammad Abu al-Aouf, head of Hamas's internal security apparatus in northern Gaza, a day after killing his commander, Naeem Muhammad Abu Nahal, who led the apparatus across Gaza, according to CNN.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the attack was one of a series of targeted killings carried out recently against members and senior officials in Hamas, adding that Israel has killed about 80 Hamas militants in the past month.

"No terrorist is immune, and no one in the Hamas leadership will manage to evade us."

— Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel

The Israeli military said Abu Nada oversaw Hamas's economic portfolio and managed its banking and investment network, directing funds toward militant activities and force buildup, and that his death may weaken the group's ability to sustain its finances. Hamas confirmed the death but had no immediate comment on the allegations about his role.

Hamas weighs its response

Hamas said the attack was the result of Israel's "policy of systematic assassinations" and warned that "targeting civilian homes constitutes a continuous breach of the ceasefire agreement in Gaza and a flagrant violation of all international and humanitarian laws, norms, and conventions." The group blamed both Israel and the US-backed Board of Peace for the ongoing attacks, saying the board "bears political and moral responsibility for the continuation of these crimes as a result of its silence and failure to halt the aggression."

The Board of Peace was established by the Trump administration and backed by a UN Security Council resolution to advance the Gaza ceasefire plan signed in October 2025, but the plan stalled within weeks of its implementation. Hamas has refused to unilaterally disarm, saying it would only do so alongside a staged Israeli withdrawal from Gaza.

Washington presses, Netanyahu holds

The strikes come as the Trump administration urges Netanyahu to proceed with the US-brokered ceasefire plan. On Tuesday, Netanyahu spoke by phone with Jared Kushner, who helped craft the deal; according to Axios, Kushner urged Netanyahu to carry out Israel's obligations under the plan, which would require Israel to stop striking Gaza and begin withdrawing forces. Netanyahu has refused to make progress on the 20-point plan until Hamas is completely disarmed, and Defense Minister Israel Katz said last week that Israel "will not withdraw from the current lines of the security zones" until Hamas is "dismantled."

The toll since the ceasefire

At least 1,600 Palestinians and 5 Israeli soldiers have been killed since the ceasefire was agreed in October 2025, according to Palestinian and Israeli tallies. Israeli troops now control around two-thirds of Gaza, up from more than half at the time of the ceasefire, with Hamas controlling a sliver of territory along Gaza's coast. Israel's assault on Gaza has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians since 2023 and led to assessments of genocide from scholars and a United Nations inquiry. Israel has denied the allegations of genocide, saying it acted in self-defence after Hamas-led militants killed 1,200 people and took more than 250 hostages in an attack on Israel in October 2023.
